title: Multiples and Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
seo_title: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find multiples of numbers up to 9; find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of numbers using the multiples method; solve problems on LCM. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on multiples and the lowest common multiple (LCM): lists of multiples, common multiples, LCM of two and three numbers and LCM word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: LCM = smallest number in both lists
key_sub: List the multiples of each number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, … (the 4 times table).
  • A common multiple is in the lists of both numbers.
  • The lowest common multiple (LCM) is the smallest common multiple.

Examples

Example

LCM of 4 and 6

4, 8, 12, …

6, 12, …

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying the numbers every time4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple, but 12 is the lowest.
Mixing up multiples and factorsMultiples get bigger: 6, 12, 18. Factors divide: 1, 2, 3, 6.
Stopping the list too earlyKeep listing until a number appears in both lists.

faq.q: What is the LCM used for?
faq.a: To find when things happen together again, and to add fractions.

faq.q: Is the LCM ever one of the numbers?
faq.a: Yes. The LCM of 3 and 6 is 6.
